claim_summary: AgenticTwin contributes a digital-twin-grounded multi-agent LLM workflow for time-series anomaly diagnosis, historical retrieval, and mitigation, together with a synthetic-anomaly benchmark.

claim_evidence.quote: To address these challenges, we propose AgenticTwin, an agentic LLM framework integrated with a DT–driven anomaly detection pipeline. Instead of relying on a single monolithic LLM, our framework decomposes anomaly reasoning into task-specific agents responsible for diagnosis, mitigation planning, and contextual historical retrieval.

modules.name: Digital-twin residual anomaly event generation
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK applies because the pipeline is built to classify normal versus abnormal sensor behavior and emit anomaly labels/events; changing the task family changes its classifier objective and event schema.

evidence.quote: The system then forms a structured anomaly event Et , consisting of the timestamp, observed values, predicted values, residuals, and predicted anomaly label.

modules.name: Historical anomaly retrieval agent
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK applies because the retrieval objective is to return similar historical anomaly cases for anomaly analysis; a different task family would require a different relevance and record-selection criterion.

evidence.quote: The RA retrieves and ranks previously observed anomaly cases that match the predicted anomaly type of the current event. Given an anomaly event Et , the RA filters the historical anomaly repository using the predicted anomaly label(s) and returns only the records that share the same anomaly type.

modules.name: Knowledge-grounded mitigation agent
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK applies because this procedure embeds the corrective-action objective for diagnosed anomalies; changing task family changes the mitigation criterion and output.

evidence.quote: The MA generates corrective actions based on the DA’s outputs, retrieved historical evidence from the RA, and anomaly taxonomy information from the curated anomaly knowledge base (KB).

modules.name: Curated anomaly knowledge base
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK applies because the taxonomy encodes anomaly-analysis concepts, symptoms, causes, and mitigations for this task family; another task family would require a different taxonomy.

evidence.quote: To support grounded anomaly reasoning, we construct a curated anomaly knowledge base (KB) that contains structured descriptions of anomaly types observed in the benchmark environment.

modules.name: Multi-agent supervisory reasoning workflow
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK applies because the workflow decomposes the anomaly diagnosis, retrieval, mitigation, and supervision objectives; changing task family changes the specialized stages and outputs.

evidence.quote: Rather than relying on a single monolithic LLM, AgenticTwin decomposes anomaly reasoning into multiple specialized agents coordinated through a supervisory architecture. Figure 4 illustrates the four-stage agentic reasoning workflow used in AgenticTwin: diagnosis, context retrieval, mitigation, and supervision.

modules.name: Synthetic anomaly and operator-query benchmark
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK applies because the benchmark hard-codes anomaly categories and diagnosis, retrieval, and mitigation query objectives; changing task family changes the injected scenarios and query suite. Its resource-level view reflects that it hosts evaluation of the workflow.

evidence.quote: Synthetic anomalies are injected into the training set to train the anomaly classifier and a separately injected held-out testing set is used for evaluation. Following the formulations introduced in Section III-C, we generate four anomaly categories: spike, drift, stuck-at, and replay.
To systematically evaluate AgenticTwin’s reasoning capabilities, we construct an LLM-assisted benchmark containing a total of 12,000 synthetic operator queries generated from anomaly events.

task_performance.quote: Table VI shows that AgenticTwin achieves the highest performance across all three tasks, obtaining diagnosis similarity, retrieval MRR, and mitigation similarity scores of 0.93, 0.95, and 0.92, respectively.

reconciliation.reason: The current module is the same contributed DT-to-event mechanism, but its old mapped status was invalid for a TSK module and its temporal data handling should be recorded explicitly.

changes: split historical retrieval, corrective-action generation, curated KB, and supervisory orchestration into separately reusable mechanisms
dimensions: Coordination and Scaling -> Planning and Orchestration where applicable
reconciliation.reason: The packet describes distinct RA, MA, KB, and supervisory workflow components. The old card combined them and omitted the explicit KB and orchestration contributions; each is independently locatable and task-bound under R3_1.

notes: The workflow is fixed because the paper specifies a four-stage diagnosis, retrieval, mitigation, and supervision sequence; agent outputs affect later content but do not select a different next tool or action. The current card omitted the contributed benchmark, knowledge-base module, and supervisory workflow and used the retired Coordination and Scaling dimension. The paper reports temporal sampling and held-out data but does not explicitly report chronology/leakage or information-cutoff checks, so temporal_validity is false.
